# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Game::placePipe
Summary: Places a pipe at the specified row and column, consuming it from the queue.
Algorithm:
  // Map player column letter 'A'...'Z' to internal index 1, 2, ...
  colIndex := col - 'A' + 1
  
  // Get current pipe from queue
  pipe := pipeQueue.peek()
  if pipe is null:
    return false
  
  // Try to place pipe on map
  success := map.tryPlacePipe(row, colIndex, pipe)
  
  if success:
    pipeQueue.consume()
    cellStack.push(map.getCell(row, colIndex)) // Assuming getCell exists or accessing via map.cell
    numOfSteps := numOfSteps + 1
    return true
  else:
    return false
Related Features: map (Map), pipeQueue (PipeQueue), cellStack (CellStack), numOfSteps (int)
Related Classes: Map, PipeQueue, CellStack, Pipe, Coordinate
Input: row (int) - The row index (1-based playable area).
       col (char) - The column letter ('A', 'B', ...).
Output: boolean - True if pipe placed successfully, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The game is in progress. Coordinates are valid for the playable area.
Post-condition: If success, pipe is removed from queue, cell is filled, step count incremented.

Game::undoStep
Summary: Undoes the last placed pipe operation.
Algorithm:

    return false // Or use a separate check for empty stack of placements

  // But CellStack tracks undo actions. We need to identify the last placed cell.
  // Based on Game::placePipe, we push to cellStack.
  if cellStack is empty:
    return false
    
  cell := cellStack.pop()
  
  // Restore pipe to queue head
  pipeQueue.undo(cell.pipe)
  
  // Clear cell on map
  map.undo(cell.coord)
  
  // Increment step count? Requirement says "increments the step count" for undoStep?
  // Requirement text: "undoStep: ... and increments the step count."
  // This implies every action (place, skip, undo) increments step count?

  numOfSteps := numOfSteps + 1
  
  return true

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation.

# Operation Specifications
Game::placePipe
Summary: Places a pipe at the specified row and column, consuming it from the queue.
Algorithm:
  1. Map player column letter to internal index: colIndex = col - 'A' + 1
  2. Peek at the current pipe from pipeQueue. If null, return false.
  3. Call map.tryPlacePipe(row, colIndex, pipe).
  4. If success:
     a. PipeQueue.consume() to remove the pipe from the queue.
     b. Get the Cell at map.cells[row][colIndex].
     c. Cast to FillableCell and push to cellStack.
     d. Increment numOfSteps by 1.
     e. Return true.
  5. If failure, return false.
Related Features: map (Map), pipeQueue (PipeQueue), cellStack (CellStack), numOfSteps (int)
Related Classes: Map, PipeQueue, CellStack, Pipe, FillableCell, Coordinate
Input: row (int) - The row index in the playable area (1..rows-2).
       col (char) - The column letter ('A', 'B', ...).
Output: boolean - True if pipe placed successfully, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The game is in progress. row is within [1..rows-2]. col represents a valid column index within [1..cols-2].
Post-condition: If true, the pipe is removed from the queue, the cell is updated with the pipe, the cell is pushed to the stack, and numOfSteps is incremented. If false, no state changes occur.

Game::undoStep
Summary: Undoes the last placed pipe operation.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if cellStack is empty (or undoCount is 0, but stack check is safer for pop).
  2. If empty, return false.
  3. Pop the last FillableCell from cellStack.
  4. Call pipeQueue.undo(cell.pipe) to return the pipe to the head of the queue.
  5. Call map.undo(cell.coord) to clear the pipe from the map cell.
  6. Increment numOfSteps by 1.
  7. Return true.
Related Features: map (Map), pipeQueue (PipeQueue), cellStack (CellStack), numOfSteps (int)
Related Classes: Map, PipeQueue, CellStack, Pipe, FillableCell, Coordinate
Input: None
Output: boolean - True if undo successful, false if no steps to undo.
Pre-condition: There is at least one step to undo (cellStack is not empty).
Post-condition: The last placed cell is cleared on the map, the pipe is returned to the queue head, and numOfSteps is incremented.

Game::hasLost
Summary: Determines if the player has lost the game.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if map.prevFilledTiles == 0.
  2. Check if delayBar.distance() > 0.
  3. If both conditions are met, return true.
  4. Otherwise, return false.
Related Features: map (Map), delayBar (DelayBar)
Related Classes: Map, DelayBar
Input: None
Output: boolean - True if the player has lost, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The game state is valid.
Post-condition: No change to system state.

Game::skipPipe
Summary: Consumes the current pipe from the queue without placing it, and increments step count.
Algorithm:
  1. Call pipeQueue.consume() to remove the top pipe from the queue.
  2. Increment numOfSteps by 1.
Related Features: pipeQueue (PipeQueue), numOfSteps (int)
Related Classes: PipeQueue, Pipe
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: The game is in progress.
Post-condition: The current pipe is removed from the queue and numOfSteps is incremented.

Game::updateState
Summary: Advances the game state by one round (delay countdown and water flow).
Algorithm:
  1. Call delayBar.countdown() to decrement the current value.
  2. Calculate dist = delayBar.distance().
  3. If dist > 0:
     a. Save the current number of filled tiles: map.prevFilledTiles = map.filledTiles.size().
     b. Call map.fillTiles(dist) to propagate water.
     c. (Optional/Implicit) Update map.prevFilledDistance if required by internal logic, though fillTiles likely handles expansion.
  4. If dist <= 0 (delay ongoing), prevFilledTiles remains unchanged or is handled by initialization.
Related Features: map (Map), delayBar (DelayBar)
Related Classes: Map, DelayBar
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: The game is in progress.
Post-condition: DelayBar is decremented. If delay has ended, water flow is advanced by the new distance, and previous filled tile count is updated for loss detection.

Game::hasWon
Summary: Determines if the player has won the game.
Algorithm:
  1. Call map.checkPath().
  2. Return the result of checkPath().
Related Features: map (Map)
Related Classes: Map
Input: None
Output: boolean - True if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The game state is valid.
Post-condition: No change to system state.

PipeQueue *-- "*" Pipe : pipeQueue
TerminationCell --|> Cell
Wall --|> Cell
@enduml
```

# Operation Specifications
Game::placePipe
Summary: Places a pipe at the specified row and column, consuming it from the queue.
Algorithm:
  1. Map player column letter to internal index: colIndex = col - 'A' + 1
  2. Peek at the current pipe from pipeQueue. If null, return false.
  3. Call map.tryPlacePipe(row, colIndex, pipe).
  4. If success:
     a. PipeQueue.consume() to remove the pipe from the queue.
     b. Get the Cell at map.cells[row][colIndex].
     c. Cast to FillableCell and push to cellStack.
     d. Increment numOfSteps by 1.
     e. Return true.
  5. If failure, return false.
Related Features: map (Map), pipeQueue (PipeQueue), cellStack (CellStack), numOfSteps (int)
Related Classes: Map, PipeQueue, CellStack, Pipe, FillableCell, Coordinate
Input: row (int) - The row index in the playable area (1..rows-2).
       col (char) - The column letter ('A', 'B', ...).
Output: boolean - True if pipe placed successfully, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The game is in progress. row is within [1..rows-2]. col represents a valid column index within [1..cols-2].
Post-condition: If true, the pipe is removed from the queue, the cell is updated with the pipe, the cell is pushed to the stack, and numOfSteps is incremented. If false, no state changes occur.

Game::undoStep
Summary: Undoes the last placed pipe operation.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if cellStack is empty (or undoCount is 0, but stack check is safer for pop).
  2. If empty, return false.
  3. Pop the last FillableCell from cellStack.
  4. Call pipeQueue.undo(cell.pipe) to return the pipe to the head of the queue.
  5. Call map.undo(cell.coord) to clear the pipe from the map cell.
  6. Increment numOfSteps by 1.
  7. Return true.
Related Features: map (Map), pipeQueue (PipeQueue), cellStack (CellStack), numOfSteps (int)
Related Classes: Map, PipeQueue, CellStack, Pipe, FillableCell, Coordinate
Input: None
Output: boolean - True if undo successful, false if no steps to undo.
Pre-condition: There is at least one step to undo (cellStack is not empty).
Post-condition: The last placed cell is cleared on the map, the pipe is returned to the queue head, and numOfSteps is incremented.

Game::hasLost
Summary: Determines if the player has lost the game.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if map.prevFilledTiles == 0.
  2. Check if delayBar.distance() > 0.
  3. If both conditions are met, return true.
  4. Otherwise, return false.
Related Features: map (Map), delayBar (DelayBar)
Related Classes: Map, DelayBar
Input: None
Output: boolean - True if the player has lost, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The game state is valid.
Post-condition: No change to system state.

Game::skipPipe
Summary: Consumes the current pipe from the queue without placing it, and increments step count.
Algorithm:
  1. Call pipeQueue.consume() to remove the top pipe from the queue.
  2. Increment numOfSteps by 1.
Related Features: pipeQueue (PipeQueue), numOfSteps (int)
Related Classes: PipeQueue, Pipe
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: The game is in progress.
Post-condition: The current pipe is removed from the queue and numOfSteps is incremented.

Game::updateState
Summary: Advances the game state by one round (delay countdown and water flow).
Algorithm:
  1. Call delayBar.countdown() to decrement the current value.
  2. Calculate dist = delayBar.distance().
  3. If dist > 0:
     a. Save the current number of filled tiles: map.prevFilledTiles = map.filledTiles.size().
     b. Call map.fillTiles(dist) to propagate water.
     c. (Optional/Implicit) Update map.prevFilledDistance if required by internal logic, though fillTiles likely handles expansion.
  4. If dist <= 0 (delay ongoing), prevFilledTiles remains unchanged or is handled by initialization.
Related Features: map (Map), delayBar (DelayBar)
Related Classes: Map, DelayBar
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: The game is in progress.
Post-condition: DelayBar is decremented. If delay has ended, water flow is advanced by the new distance, and previous filled tile count is updated for loss detection.

Game::hasWon
Summary: Determines if the player has won the game.
Algorithm:
  1. Call map.checkPath().
  2. Return the result of checkPath().
Related Features: map (Map)
Related Classes: Map
Input: None
Output: boolean - True if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The game state is valid.
Post-condition: No change to system state.

   *   4. If dist <= 0, no water flow occurs, but countdown still happens.
   * Related Features: map (Map), delayBar (DelayBar)
   * Related Classes: Map, DelayBar
   * Input: None
   * Output: void
   * Pre-condition: The game is in progress.

    public boolean placePipe(final int row, final char col) {
        int colIndex = col - 'A' + 1;
        Pipe pipe = getPipeQueue().peek();
        if (pipe == null) { // Should not happen if game is in progress and queue is managed
            return false;
        }
        boolean success = getMap().tryPlacePipe(row, colIndex, pipe);
        if (success) {
            getPipeQueue().consume();
            Cell cell = getMap().getCell()[row][colIndex];
            if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
                FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) cell;
                getCellStack().push(fillableCell);
                setNumOfSteps(getNumOfSteps() + 1);
                return true;
            } else {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return false;
    }
    public void skipPipe() {
        getPipeQueue().consume();
        setNumOfSteps(getNumOfSteps() + 1);
    }
    public boolean undoStep() {
        if (getCellStack().getCount() == 0) {
            return false;
        }
        FillableCell cell = getCellStack().pop();
        getPipeQueue().undo(cell.getPipe());
        // Assuming getCoord() exists based on docstring
        getMap().undo(cell.getCoord());
        setNumOfSteps(getNumOfSteps() + 1);
        return true;
    }
    public void updateState() {
        getDelayBar().countdown();
        int dist = getDelayBar().distance();
        if (dist > 0) {
            getMap().setPrevFilledTiles(getMap().getFilledTiles().size());
            getMap().fillTiles(dist);
        }
    }
    public boolean hasWon() {
        return getMap().checkPath();
    }
    public boolean hasLost() {
        if (getMap().getPrevFilledTiles() == 0 && getDelayBar().distance() > 0) {
            return true;
        }
        return false;
    }

1. Compute context information
  1.1 Navigate the Ecore model to find related classes
  1.2 Also consider the related classes in the Javadocs.
  1.3 Locate these files in your project.
  1.4 Generate the class summarization.
2. A method is unimplemented if its body contains `// TODO: Please complete this Java method based on the docstring`.
3. For every unimplemented method, 
  3.1 You must read the docstring of this method. The fragment between `<!-- begin-model-doc -->` and `<!-- end-model-doc -->` contains the method specification;
  3.2 Generate your code strictly according to the algorithm; Be aware of the EMF code style and APIs;
  3.3 You should not change the method signature;
  3.4 After generation, replace the current body with the one you generate;
  3.5 Keep and update the docstring by changing `@generated` to `@generated NOT`.
4. Check the import list. Add missing imports if needed.
5. Do not change other part.
6. Be aware of the method signatures, particularly, the input and output types, provided in the **Context**.

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT

  public void undo(final Coordinate coord)

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Fills pipes within the specified distance from source using BFS-style expansion.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If sourceCell is null or not filled, return.
   *   2. Determine the new layer to fill. 
   *      - If distance <= prevFilledDistance, return (already filled).
   *      - Let stepsToAdd = distance - prevFilledDistance.
   *   3. Initialize BFS from the current filledTiles.
   *      - currentFrontier := new List<Coordinate>(filledTiles)
   *      - nextFrontier := List<Coordinate>()
   *      - newlyFilledTiles := List<Coordinate>()
   *   
   *   4. Repeat 'stepsToAdd' times:
   *      a. For each coord in currentFrontier:
   *         i.   Get the cell at coord.
   *         ii.  Get the connections of the cell's pipe (or source/sink direction).
   *         iii. For each direction d in connections:
   *              - offset := Pa19Helper.getOffset(d)
   *              - nextCoord := coord.add(offset)
   *              - If nextCoord is within playable bounds [1..rows-2] x [1..cols-2]:
   *                  - Get neighborCell at nextCoord.
   *                  - Check if neighborCell is valid for connection:
   *                      - It must be a FillableCell or TerminationCell.
   *                      - It must not be already in filledTiles (or newlyFilledTiles).
   *                      - It must have a pipe/termination that connects back to 'd' (i.e., its connection opposite to 'd' is valid).
   *                  - If valid:
   *                      - Add nextCoord to nextFrontier and newlyFilledTiles.
   *                      - Mark neighborCell as filled (if TerminationCell, set filled=true; if FillableCell, it is already filled by being placed? No, FillableCell pipe exists, but "filled" state might be implicit or explicit. Requirement: "fillBeginTile() marks source... filled". FillableCell has `pipe.filled`. TerminationCell has `filled`. 
   *                      - Note: Requirement says "fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled". For pipes, they are filled when water reaches them. The `Pipe` object has a `filled` boolean. The `TerminationCell` has a `filled` boolean.
   *                      - Set neighborCell.filled = true.
   *      b. currentFrontier := nextFrontier
   *      c. If currentFrontier is empty, break.
   *   
   *   5. Add all newlyFilledTiles to filledTiles.
   *   6. Update prevFilledDistance := distance.
   *   7. Update prevFilledTiles := newlyFilledTiles.size().
   * Related Features: filledTiles, prevFilledDistance, prevFilledTiles, sourceCell, cells
   * Related Classes: Coordinate, Pipe, TerminationCell, FillableCell, Pa19Helper
   * Input: distance (int) - The total distance from source to fill up to.
   * Output: None
   * Pre-condition: sourceCell is filled.
   * Post-condition: filledTiles contains all cells reachable within 'distance' hops. prevFilledTiles records the count of newly filled tiles in this step.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public void fillTiles(final int distance)
  {
    // 1. If sourceCell is null or not filled, return.
    if (sourceCell == null || !sourceCell.isFilled()) {
      return;
    }

    // 2. Determine the new layer to fill.
    int prevDist = prevFilledDistance == null ? 0 : prevFilledDistance;
    if (distance <= prevDist) {
      return;
    }
    int stepsToAdd = distance - prevDist;

    // 3. Initialize BFS
    List<Coordinate> currentFrontier = new ArrayList<>(filledTiles);
    List<Coordinate> nextFrontier = new ArrayList<>();
    List<Coordinate> newlyFilledTiles = new ArrayList<>();

    // 4. Repeat 'stepsToAdd' times
    for (int step = 0; step < stepsToAdd; step++) {
      List<Coordinate> tempFrontier = new ArrayList<>();
      
      for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
        Cell cell = this.cell[coord.getRow()][coord.getCol()];
        
        // Determine connections
        List<Integer> connections = new ArrayList<>();
        if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
          Pipe pipe = ((FillableCell) cell).getPipe();
          if (pipe != null) {
            connections.addAll(pipe.getDirections()); // Assuming getDirections() or getConnections()
          }
        } else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
          // Termination cells might have a direction
          connections.add(((TerminationCell) cell).getDirection()); 
        }

        for (int d : connections) {
          Coordinate offset = Pa19Helper.getOffset(d);
          Coordinate nextCoord = coord.add(offset);

          // Check bounds
          if (nextCoord.isValid(getRows(), getCols())) { // Assuming isValid checks [1, rows-2] etc.
            // If not, manual check:
            if (nextCoord.getRow() >= 1 && nextCoord.getRow() < getRows() - 1 &&
                nextCoord.getCol() >= 1 && nextCoord.getCol() < getCols() - 1) {
              
              Cell neighborCell = this.cell[nextCoord.getRow()][nextCoord.getCol()];

              // Check if already filled
              if (!isFilled(nextCoord)) {
                
                // Check connection validity
                if (isValidConnection(neighborCell, d)) {
                  nextFrontier.add(nextCoord);
                  newlyFilledTiles.add(nextCoord);
                  
                  // Mark as filled
                  if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                     Pipe neighborPipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
                     if (neighborPipe != null) {
                       neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
                     }
                  } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                     ((TerminationCell) neighborCell).setFilled(true);
                  }
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
      
      currentFrontier = nextFrontier;
      nextFrontier = new ArrayList<>(); // Reset nextFrontier for next step
      
      if (currentFrontier.isEmpty()) {
        break;
      }
    }

    // 5. Add all newlyFilledTiles to filledTiles
    filledTiles.addAll(newlyFilledTiles);

    // 6. Update prevFilledDistance
    prevFilledDistance = distance;

    // 7. Update prevFilledTiles
    prevFilledTiles = newlyFilledTiles.size();
  }

  /**
   * Helper method to check if a coordinate is already filled
   */
  private boolean isFilled(Coordinate coord) {
    return filledTiles.contains(coord);
  }

  /**
   * Helper method to check if a neighbor cell is valid for connection in direction d
   */
  private boolean isValidConnection(Cell neighborCell, int direction) {
    if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
      Pipe pipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
      if (pipe == null) {
        return false;
      }
      // Check if the pipe has an opening in the opposite direction
      int oppositeDirection = Pa19Helper.getOppositeDirection(direction);
      return pipe.getDirections().contains(oppositeDirection);
    } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
      // TerminationCell connects if its direction matches the incoming direction
      // Or if it's a sink/source that accepts water
      int neighborDir = ((TerminationCell) neighborCell).getDirection();
      return neighborDir == Pa19Helper.getOppositeDirection(direction);
    }
    return false;
  }

   * Summary: Fills pipes within the specified distance from source using BFS-style expansion.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If sourceCell is null or not filled, return.
   *   2. Determine the new layer to fill.

   *      - Let stepsToAdd = distance - prevFilledDistance.
   *   3. Initialize BFS from the current filledTiles.
   *      - currentFrontier := new List<Coordinate>(filledTiles)
   *      - nextFrontier := List<Coordinate>()
   *      - newlyFilledTiles := List<Coordinate>()
   *   
   *   4. Repeat 'stepsToAdd' times:
   *      a. For each coord in currentFrontier:
   *         i.   Get the cell at coord.
   *         ii.  Get the connections of the cell's pipe (or source/sink direction).
   *         iii. For each direction d in connections:
   *              - offset := Pa19Helper.getOffset(d)
   *              - nextCoord := coord.add(offset)
   *              - If nextCoord is within playable bounds [1..rows-2] x [1..cols-2]:
   *                  - Get neighborCell at nextCoord.
   *                  - Check if neighborCell is valid for connection:
   *                      - It must be a FillableCell or TerminationCell.
   *                      - It must not be already in filledTiles (or newlyFilledTiles).
   *                      - It must have a pipe/termination that connects back to 'd' (i.e., its connection opposite to 'd' is valid).
   *                  - If valid:
   *                      - Add nextCoord to nextFrontier and newlyFilledTiles.

No, FillableCell pipe exists, but "filled" state might be implicit or explicit. Requirement: "fillBeginTile() marks source... filled". FillableCell has `pipe.filled`. TerminationCell has `filled`. 
   *                      - Note: Requirement says "fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled". For pipes, they are filled when water reaches them. The `Pipe` object has a `filled` boolean. The `TerminationCell` has a `filled` boolean.
   *                      - Set neighborCell.filled = true.
   *      b. currentFrontier := nextFrontier
   *      c. If currentFrontier is empty, break.

   *   7. Update prevFilledTiles := newlyFilledTiles.size().

   * Related Classes: Coordinate, Pipe, TerminationCell, FillableCell, Pa19Helper
   * Input: distance (int) - The total distance from source to fill up to.
   * Output: None
   * Pre-condition: sourceCell is filled.
   * Post-condition: filledTiles contains all cells reachable within 'distance' hops. prevFilledTiles records the count of newly filled tiles in this step.

   * <!-- end-user-doc -->

   * Summary: Fills pipes within the specified distance from source using BFS-style expansion.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If sourceCell is null or not filled, return.
   *   2. Determine the new layer to fill. 
   *      - If distance <= prevFilledDistance, return (already filled).
   *      - Let stepsToAdd = distance - prevFilledDistance.
   *   3. Initialize BFS from the current filledTiles.
   *      - currentFrontier := new List<Coordinate>(filledTiles)
   *      - nextFrontier := List<Coordinate>()
   *      - newlyFilledTiles := List<Coordinate>()
   *   
   *   4. Repeat 'stepsToAdd' times:
   *      a. For each coord in currentFrontier:
   *         i.   Get the cell at coord.
   *         ii.  Get the connections of the cell's pipe (or source/sink direction).
   *         iii. For each direction d in connections:
   *              - offset := Pa19Helper.getOffset(d)
   *              - nextCoord := coord.add(offset)
   *              - If nextCoord is within playable bounds [1..rows-2] x [1..cols-2]:
   *                  - Get neighborCell at nextCoord.
   *                  - Check if neighborCell is valid for connection:
   *                      - It must be a FillableCell or TerminationCell.
   *                      - It must not be already in filledTiles (or newlyFilledTiles).
   *                      - It must have a pipe/termination that connects back to 'd' (i.e., its connection opposite to 'd' is valid).
   *                  - If valid:
   *                      - Add nextCoord to nextFrontier and newlyFilledTiles.
   *                      - Mark neighborCell as filled (if TerminationCell, set filled=true; if FillableCell, it is already filled by being placed? No, FillableCell pipe exists, but "filled" state might be implicit or explicit. Requirement: "fillBeginTile() marks source... filled". FillableCell has `pipe.filled`. TerminationCell has `filled`. 
   *                      - Note: Requirement says "fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled". For pipes, they are filled when water reaches them. The `Pipe` object has a `filled` boolean. The `TerminationCell` has a `filled` boolean.
   *                      - Set neighborCell.filled = true.
   *      b. currentFrontier := nextFrontier
   *      c. If currentFrontier is empty, break.
   *   
   *   5. Add all newlyFilledTiles to filledTiles.
   *   6. Update prevFilledDistance := distance.
   *   7. Update prevFilledTiles := newlyFilledTiles.size().
   * Related Features: filledTiles, prevFilledDistance, prevFilledTiles, sourceCell, cells
   * Related Classes: Coordinate, Pipe, TerminationCell, FillableCell, Pa19Helper
   * Input: distance (int) - The total distance from source to fill up to.
   * Output: None
   * Pre-condition: sourceCell is filled.
   * Post-condition: filledTiles contains all cells reachable within 'distance' hops. prevFilledTiles records the count of newly filled tiles in this step.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public void fillTiles(final int distance)
  {
    // 1. If sourceCell is null or not filled, return.
    if (sourceCell == null || !sourceCell.isFilled()) {
      return;
    }

    // 2. Determine the new layer to fill.
    int prevDist = prevFilledDistance == null ? 0 : prevFilledDistance;
    if (distance <= prevDist) {
      return;
    }
    int stepsToAdd = distance - prevDist;

    // 3. Initialize BFS
    List<Coordinate> currentFrontier = new ArrayList<>(filledTiles);
    List<Coordinate> nextFrontier = new ArrayList<>();
    List<Coordinate> newlyFilledTiles = new ArrayList<>();

    // 4. Repeat 'stepsToAdd' times
    for (int step = 0; step < stepsToAdd; step++) {
      List<Coordinate> tempFrontier = new ArrayList<>();
      
      for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
        Cell cell = this.cell[coord.getRow()][coord.getCol()];
        
        // Determine connections
        List<Integer> connections = new ArrayList<>();
        if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
          Pipe pipe = ((FillableCell) cell).getPipe();
          if (pipe != null) {
            connections.addAll(pipe.getDirections()); // Assuming getDirections() or getConnections()
          }
        } else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
          // Termination cells might have a direction
          connections.add(((TerminationCell) cell).getDirection()); 
        }

        for (int d : connections) {
          Coordinate offset = Pa19Helper.getOffset(d);
          Coordinate nextCoord = coord.add(offset);

          // Check bounds
          if (nextCoord.isValid(getRows(), getCols())) { // Assuming isValid checks [1, rows-2] etc.
            // If not, manual check:
            if (nextCoord.getRow() >= 1 && nextCoord.getRow() < getRows() - 1 &&
                nextCoord.getCol() >= 1 && nextCoord.getCol() < getCols() - 1) {
              
              Cell neighborCell = this.cell[nextCoord.getRow()][nextCoord.getCol()];

              // Check if already filled
              if (!isFilled(nextCoord)) {
                
                // Check connection validity
                if (isValidConnection(neighborCell, d)) {
                  nextFrontier.add(nextCoord);
                  newlyFilledTiles.add(nextCoord);
                  
                  // Mark as filled
                  if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                     Pipe neighborPipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
                     if (neighborPipe != null) {
                       neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
                     }
                  } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                     ((TerminationCell) neighborCell).setFilled(true);
                  }
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
      
      currentFrontier = nextFrontier;
      nextFrontier = new ArrayList<>(); // Reset nextFrontier for next step
      
      if (currentFrontier.isEmpty()) {
        break;
      }
    }

    // 5. Add all newlyFilledTiles to filledTiles
    filledTiles.addAll(newlyFilledTiles);

    // 6. Update prevFilledDistance
    prevFilledDistance = distance;

    // 7. Update prevFilledTiles
    prevFilledTiles = newlyFilledTiles.size();
  }

   * Helper method to check if a neighbor cell is valid for connection in direction d
   * @LLM */
  private boolean isValidConnection(Cell neighborCell, int direction) {
    if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
      Pipe pipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
      if (pipe == null) {
        return false;
      }
      // Check if the pipe has an opening in the opposite direction
      int oppositeDirection = Pa19Helper.getOppositeDirection(direction);
      return pipe.getDirections().contains(oppositeDirection);
    } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
      // TerminationCell connects if its direction matches the incoming direction
      // Or if it's a sink/source that accepts water
      int neighborDir = ((TerminationCell) neighborCell).getDirection();
      return neighborDir == Pa19Helper.getOppositeDirection(direction);
    }
    return false;
  }

   *   2. Determine the new layer to fill. 
   *      - If distance <= prevFilledDistance, return (already filled).
   *      - Let stepsToAdd = distance - prevFilledDistance.
   *   3. Initialize BFS from the current filledTiles.
   *      - currentFrontier := new List<Coordinate>(filledTiles)
   *      - nextFrontier := List<Coordinate>()
   *      - newlyFilledTiles := List<Coordinate>()
   *   
   *   4. Repeat 'stepsToAdd' times:
   *      a. For each coord in currentFrontier:
   *         i.   Get the cell at coord.
   *         ii.  Get the connections of the cell's pipe (or source/sink direction).
   *         iii. For each direction d in connections:
   *              - offset := Pa19Helper.getOffset(d)
   *              - nextCoord := coord.add(offset)
   *              - If nextCoord is within playable bounds [1..rows-2] x [1..cols-2]:
   *                  - Get neighborCell at nextCoord.
   *                  - Check if neighborCell is valid for connection:
   *                      - It must be a FillableCell or TerminationCell.
   *                      - It must not be already in filledTiles (or newlyFilledTiles).
   *                      - It must have a pipe/termination that connects back to 'd' (i.e., its connection opposite to 'd' is valid).
   *                  - If valid:
   *                      - Add nextCoord to nextFrontier and newlyFilledTiles.
   *                      - Mark neighborCell as filled (if TerminationCell, set filled=true; if FillableCell, it is already filled by being placed? No, FillableCell pipe exists, but "filled" state might be implicit or explicit. Requirement: "fillBeginTile() marks source... filled". FillableCell has `pipe.filled`. TerminationCell has `filled`. 
   *                      - Note: Requirement says "fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled". For pipes, they are filled when water reaches them. The `Pipe` object has a `filled` boolean. The `TerminationCell` has a `filled` boolean.
   *                      - Set neighborCell.filled = true.
   *      b. currentFrontier := nextFrontier
   *      c. If currentFrontier is empty, break.
   *   
   *   5. Add all newlyFilledTiles to filledTiles.
   *   6. Update prevFilledDistance := distance.
   *   7. Update prevFilledTiles := newlyFilledTiles.size().
   * Related Features: filledTiles, prevFilledDistance, prevFilledTiles, sourceCell, cells
   * Related Classes: Coordinate, Pipe, TerminationCell, FillableCell, Pa19Helper
   * Input: distance (int) - The total distance from source to fill up to.
   * Output: None
   * Pre-condition: sourceCell is filled.
   * Post-condition: filledTiles contains all cells reachable within 'distance' hops. prevFilledTiles records the count of newly filled tiles in this step.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public void fillTiles(final int distance)
  {
    // 1. If sourceCell is null or not filled, return.
    if (sourceCell == null || !sourceCell.isFilled()) {
      return;
    }

    // 2. Determine the new layer to fill.
    int prevDist = prevFilledDistance == null ? 0 : prevFilledDistance;
    if (distance <= prevDist) {
      return;
    }
    int stepsToAdd = distance - prevDist;

    // 3. Initialize BFS
    List<Coordinate> currentFrontier = new ArrayList<>(filledTiles);
    List<Coordinate> nextFrontier = new ArrayList<>();
    List<Coordinate> newlyFilledTiles = new ArrayList<>();

    // 4. Repeat 'stepsToAdd' times
    for (int step = 0; step < stepsToAdd; step++) {
      List<Coordinate> tempFrontier = new ArrayList<>();
      
      for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
        Cell cell = this.cell[coord.getRow()][coord.getCol()];
        
        // Determine connections
        List<Integer> connections = new ArrayList<>();
        if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
          Pipe pipe = ((FillableCell) cell).getPipe();
          if (pipe != null) {
            connections.addAll(pipe.getDirections()); // Assuming getDirections() or getConnections()
          }
        } else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
          // Termination cells might have a direction
          connections.add(((TerminationCell) cell).getDirection()); 
        }

        for (int d : connections) {
          Coordinate offset = Pa19Helper.getOffset(d);
          Coordinate nextCoord = coord.add(offset);

          // Check bounds
          if (nextCoord.isValid(getRows(), getCols())) { // Assuming isValid checks [1, rows-2] etc.
            // If not, manual check:
            if (nextCoord.getRow() >= 1 && nextCoord.getRow() < getRows() - 1 &&
                nextCoord.getCol() >= 1 && nextCoord.getCol() < getCols() - 1) {
              
              Cell neighborCell = this.cell[nextCoord.getRow()][nextCoord.getCol()];

              // Check if already filled
              if (!isFilled(nextCoord)) {
                
                // Check connection validity
                if (isValidConnection(neighborCell, d)) {
                  nextFrontier.add(nextCoord);
                  newlyFilledTiles.add(nextCoord);
                  
                  // Mark as filled
                  if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                     Pipe neighborPipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
                     if (neighborPipe != null) {
                       neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
                     }
                  } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                     ((TerminationCell) neighborCell).setFilled(true);
                  }
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
      
      currentFrontier = nextFrontier;
      nextFrontier = new ArrayList<>(); // Reset nextFrontier for next step
      
      if (currentFrontier.isEmpty()) {
        break;
      }
    }

    // 5. Add all newlyFilledTiles to filledTiles
    filledTiles.addAll(newlyFilledTiles);

    // 6. Update prevFilledDistance
    prevFilledDistance = distance;

    // 7. Update prevFilledTiles
    prevFilledTiles = newlyFilledTiles.size();
  }

  /**
   * Helper method to check if a neighbor cell is valid for connection in direction d
   * @LLM */
  private boolean isValidConnection(Cell neighborCell, int direction) {
    if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
      Pipe pipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
      if (pipe == null) {
        return false;
      }
      // Check if the pipe has an opening in the opposite direction
      int oppositeDirection = Pa19Helper.getOppositeDirection(direction);
      return pipe.getDirections().contains(oppositeDirection);
    } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
      // TerminationCell connects if its direction matches the incoming direction
      // Or if it's a sink/source that accepts water
      int neighborDir = ((TerminationCell) neighborCell).getDirection();
      return neighborDir == Pa19Helper.getOppositeDirection(direction);
    }
    return false;
  }

   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Fills pipes within the specified distance from source using BFS-style expansion.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If sourceCell is null or not filled, return.
   *   2. Determine the new layer to fill. 
   *      - If distance <= prevFilledDistance, return (already filled).
   *      - Let stepsToAdd = distance - prevFilledDistance.
   *   3. Initialize BFS from the current filledTiles.
   *      - currentFrontier := new List<Coordinate>(filledTiles)
   *      - nextFrontier := List<Coordinate>()
   *      - newlyFilledTiles := List<Coordinate>()
   *   
   *   4. Repeat 'stepsToAdd' times:
   *      a. For each coord in currentFrontier:
   *         i.   Get the cell at coord.
   *         ii.  Get the connections of the cell's pipe (or source/sink direction).
   *         iii. For each direction d in connections:
   *              - offset := Pa19Helper.getOffset(d)
   *              - nextCoord := coord.add(offset)
   *              - If nextCoord is within playable bounds [1..rows-2] x [1..cols-2]:
   *                  - Get neighborCell at nextCoord.
   *                  - Check if neighborCell is valid for connection:
   *                      - It must be a FillableCell or TerminationCell.
   *                      - It must not be already in filledTiles (or newlyFilledTiles).
   *                      - It must have a pipe/termination that connects back to 'd' (i.e., its connection opposite to 'd' is valid).
   *                  - If valid:
   *                      - Add nextCoord to nextFrontier and newlyFilledTiles.
   *                      - Mark neighborCell as filled (if TerminationCell, set filled=true; if FillableCell, it is already filled by being placed? No, FillableCell pipe exists, but "filled" state might be implicit or explicit. Requirement: "fillBeginTile() marks source... filled". FillableCell has `pipe.filled`. TerminationCell has `filled`. 
   *                      - Note: Requirement says "fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled". For pipes, they are filled when water reaches them. The `Pipe` object has a `filled` boolean. The `TerminationCell` has a `filled` boolean.
   *                      - Set neighborCell.filled = true.
   *      b. currentFrontier := nextFrontier
   *      c. If currentFrontier is empty, break.
   *   
   *   5. Add all newlyFilledTiles to filledTiles.
   *   6. Update prevFilledDistance := distance.
   *   7. Update prevFilledTiles := newlyFilledTiles.size().
   * Related Features: filledTiles, prevFilledDistance, prevFilledTiles, sourceCell, cells
   * Related Classes: Coordinate, Pipe, TerminationCell, FillableCell, Pa19Helper
   * Input: distance (int) - The total distance from source to fill up to.
   * Output: None
   * Pre-condition: sourceCell is filled.
   * Post-condition: filledTiles contains all cells reachable within 'distance' hops. prevFilledTiles records the count of newly filled tiles in this step.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public void fillTiles(final int distance)
  {
    // 1. If sourceCell is null or not filled, return.
    if (sourceCell == null || !sourceCell.isFilled()) {
      return;
    }

    // 2. Determine the new layer to fill.
    int prevDist = prevFilledDistance == null ? 0 : prevFilledDistance;
    if (distance <= prevDist) {
      return;
    }
    int stepsToAdd = distance - prevDist;

    // 3. Initialize BFS
    List<Coordinate> currentFrontier = new ArrayList<>(filledTiles);
    List<Coordinate> nextFrontier = new ArrayList<>();
    List<Coordinate> newlyFilledTiles = new ArrayList<>();

    // 4. Repeat 'stepsToAdd' times
    for (int step = 0; step < stepsToAdd; step++) {
      List<Coordinate> tempFrontier = new ArrayList<>();
      
      for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
        Cell cell = this.cell[coord.getRow()][coord.getCol()];
        
        // Determine connections
        List<Integer> connections = new ArrayList<>();
        if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
          Pipe pipe = ((FillableCell) cell).getPipe();
          if (pipe != null) {
            connections.addAll(pipe.getDirections()); // Assuming getDirections() or getConnections()
          }
        } else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
          // Termination cells might have a direction
          connections.add(((TerminationCell) cell).getDirection()); 
        }

        for (int d : connections) {
          Coordinate offset = Pa19Helper.getOffset(d);
          Coordinate nextCoord = coord.add(offset);

          // Check bounds
          if (nextCoord.isValid(getRows(), getCols())) { // Assuming isValid checks [1, rows-2] etc.
            // If not, manual check:
            if (nextCoord.getRow() >= 1 && nextCoord.getRow() < getRows() - 1 &&
                nextCoord.getCol() >= 1 && nextCoord.getCol() < getCols() - 1) {
              
              Cell neighborCell = this.cell[nextCoord.getRow()][nextCoord.getCol()];

              // Check if already filled
              if (!isFilled(nextCoord)) {
                
                // Check connection validity
                if (isValidConnection(neighborCell, d)) {
                  nextFrontier.add(nextCoord);
                  newlyFilledTiles.add(nextCoord);
                  
                  // Mark as filled
                  if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                     Pipe neighborPipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
                     if (neighborPipe != null) {
                       neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
                     }
                  } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                     ((TerminationCell) neighborCell).setFilled(true);
                  }
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
      
      currentFrontier = nextFrontier;
      nextFrontier = new ArrayList<>(); // Reset nextFrontier for next step
      
      if (currentFrontier.isEmpty()) {
        break;
      }
    }

    // 5. Add all newlyFilledTiles to filledTiles
    filledTiles.addAll(newlyFilledTiles);

    // 6. Update prevFilledDistance
    prevFilledDistance = distance;

    // 7. Update prevFilledTiles
    prevFilledTiles = newlyFilledTiles.size();
  }

  /**
   * Helper method to check if a neighbor cell is valid for connection in direction d
   * @LLM */
  private boolean isValidConnection(Cell neighborCell, int direction) {
    if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
      Pipe pipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
      if (pipe == null) {
        return false;
      }
      // Check if the pipe has an opening in the opposite direction
      int oppositeDirection = Pa19Helper.getOppositeDirection(direction);
      return pipe.getDirections().contains(oppositeDirection);
    } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
      // TerminationCell connects if its direction matches the incoming direction
      // Or if it's a sink/source that accepts water
      int neighborDir = ((TerminationCell) neighborCell).getDirection();
      return neighborDir == Pa19Helper.getOppositeDirection(direction);
    }
    return false;
  }

   * Helper method to check if a neighbor cell is valid for connection in direction d

  private boolean isValidConnection(Cell neighborCell, Direction direction) { // Fixed: direction is Direction
    if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
      Pipe pipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
      if (pipe == null) {
        return false;
      }
      // Check if the pipe has an opening in the opposite direction
      Direction oppositeDirection = Pa19Helper.getOppositeDirection(direction); // Fixed: getOppositeDirection takes Direction
      return pipe.getConnections().contains(oppositeDirection); // Fixed: getConnections()
    } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
      // TerminationCell connects if its direction matches the incoming direction
      // Or if it's a sink/source that accepts water
      Direction neighborDir = ((TerminationCell) neighborCell).getConnection(); // Fixed: getConnection()
      return neighborDir == Pa19Helper.getOppositeDirection(direction); // Fixed: getOppositeDirection takes Direction
    }
    return false;
  }

  {

    }

    // 2. Determine the new layer to fill.
    int prevDist = prevFilledDistance == null ? 0 : prevFilledDistance;
    if (distance <= prevDist) {
      return;
    }
    int stepsToAdd = distance - prevDist;

    // 3. Initialize BFS
    List<Coordinate> currentFrontier = new ArrayList<>(filledTiles);
    List<Coordinate> nextFrontier = new ArrayList<>();
    List<Coordinate> newlyFilledTiles = new ArrayList<>();

    // 4. Repeat 'stepsToAdd' times
    for (int step = 0; step < stepsToAdd; step++) {
      List<Coordinate> tempFrontier = new ArrayList<>();
      
      for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
        Cell cell = this.cell[coord.getRow()][coord.getCol()];
        
        // Determine connections
        List<Integer> connections = new ArrayList<>();
        if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
          Pipe pipe = ((FillableCell) cell).getPipe();
          if (pipe != null) {
            connections.addAll(pipe.getDirections()); // Assuming getDirections() or getConnections()
          }
        } else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
          // Termination cells might have a direction
          connections.add(((TerminationCell) cell).getDirection()); 
        }

        for (int d : connections) {
          Coordinate offset = Pa19Helper.getOffset(d);
          Coordinate nextCoord = coord.add(offset);

          // Check bounds

                     if (neighborPipe != null) {
                       neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
                     }
                  } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                     ((TerminationCell) neighborCell).setFilled(true);
                  }
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }

      nextFrontier = new ArrayList<>(); // Reset nextFrontier for next step

      }

        if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
          Pipe pipe = ((FillableCell) cell).getPipe();
          if (pipe != null) {
            // Convert Integer directions to Direction enum
            for (Integer dInt : pipe.getDirections()) {
                connections.add(Direction.values()[dInt]);
            }
          }
        } else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
          // Use getDirection() instead of getConnection()
          connections.add(((TerminationCell) cell).getDirection()); 
        }

        for (Direction dir : connections) {
          Coordinate offset = helper.getOffset(dir); // Fixed: non-static method
          Coordinate nextCoord = coord.add(offset);

          // Check bounds
          if (nextCoord.isValid(getRows(), getCols())) { 
            // Manual check as fallback or primary if isValid is unreliable
            if (nextCoord.getRow() >= 1 && nextCoord.getRow() < getRows() - 1 &&
                nextCoord.getCol() >= 1 && nextCoord.getCol() < getCols() - 1) {
              
              Cell neighborCell = this.cell[nextCoord.getRow()][nextCoord.getCol()];

              // Check if already filled
              if (!isFilled(nextCoord)) {
                
                // Check connection validity
                if (isValidConnection(neighborCell, dir, helper)) {
                  nextFrontier.add(nextCoord);
                  newlyFilledTiles.add(nextCoord);
                  
                  // Mark as filled
                  if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                     Pipe neighborPipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
                     if (neighborPipe != null) {
                       neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
                     }
                  } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                     ((TerminationCell) neighborCell).setFilled(true);
                  }
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
      
      currentFrontier = nextFrontier;
      nextFrontier = new ArrayList<>(); // Reset nextFrontier for next step
      
      if (currentFrontier.isEmpty()) {
        break;
      }
    }

    // 5. Add all newlyFilledTiles to filledTiles
    filledTiles.addAll(newlyFilledTiles);

    // 6. Update prevFilledDistance
    prevFilledDistance = distance;

    // 7. Update prevFilledTiles
    prevFilledTiles = newlyFilledTiles.size();
  }

  /**
   * Helper method to check if a neighbor cell is valid for connection in direction d
   * @LLM */
  private boolean isValidConnection(Cell neighborCell, Direction direction, Pa19Helper helper) {
    if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
      Pipe pipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
      if (pipe == null) {
        return false;
      }
      // Check if the pipe has an opening in the opposite direction
      Direction oppositeDirection = helper.getOpposite(direction); // Fixed: method name and instance call
      // Check if pipe contains this direction
      for (Integer dInt : pipe.getDirections()) {
          if (Direction.values()[dInt] == oppositeDirection) {
              return true;
          }
      }
      return false;
    } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
      // TerminationCell connects if its direction matches the incoming direction
      Direction neighborDir = ((TerminationCell) neighborCell).getDirection(); // Fixed: getDirection instead of getConnection
      Direction oppositeDirection = helper.getOpposite(direction); // Fixed: method name and instance call
      return neighborDir == oppositeDirection;
    }
    return false;
  }

- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

   *              - nextCoord := coord.add(offset)
   *              - If nextCoord is within playable bounds [1..rows-2] x [1..cols-2]:

   *                      - It must not be already in filledTiles (or newlyFilledTiles).

  {
    // 1. If sourceCell is null or not filled, return.
    if (sourceCell == null || !sourceCell.isFilled()) {
      return;
    }

    // 2. Determine the new layer to fill.
    int prevDist = prevFilledDistance == null ? 0 : prevFilledDistance;
    if (distance <= prevDist) {
      return;
    }
    int stepsToAdd = distance - prevDist;

    // 3. Initialize BFS
    List<Coordinate> currentFrontier = new ArrayList<>(filledTiles);
    List<Coordinate> nextFrontier = new ArrayList<>();
    List<Coordinate> newlyFilledTiles = new ArrayList<>();

    // 4. Repeat 'stepsToAdd' times
    for (int step = 0; step < stepsToAdd; step++) {
      List<Coordinate> tempFrontier = new ArrayList<>();
      
      for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
        Cell cell = this.cell[coord.getRow()][coord.getCol()];
        
        // Determine connections
        List<Integer> connections = new ArrayList<>();
        if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
          Pipe pipe = ((FillableCell) cell).getPipe();
          if (pipe != null) {
            connections.addAll(pipe.getDirections()); // Assuming getDirections() or getConnections()
          }
        } else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
          // Termination cells might have a direction
          connections.add(((TerminationCell) cell).getDirection()); 
        }

        for (int d : connections) {
          Coordinate offset = Pa19Helper.getOffset(d);
          Coordinate nextCoord = coord.add(offset);

          // Check bounds
          if (nextCoord.isValid(getRows(), getCols())) { // Assuming isValid checks [1, rows-2] etc.
            // If not, manual check:
            if (nextCoord.getRow() >= 1 && nextCoord.getRow() < getRows() - 1 &&
                nextCoord.getCol() >= 1 && nextCoord.getCol() < getCols() - 1) {

              // Check if already filled

                // Check connection validity
                if (isValidConnection(neighborCell, d)) {
                  nextFrontier.add(nextCoord);
                  newlyFilledTiles.add(nextCoord);
                  
                  // Mark as filled
                  if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                     Pipe neighborPipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
                     if (neighborPipe != null) {
                       neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
                     }
                  } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                     ((TerminationCell) neighborCell).setFilled(true);
                  }
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
      
      currentFrontier = nextFrontier;
      nextFrontier = new ArrayList<>(); // Reset nextFrontier for next step
      
      if (currentFrontier.isEmpty()) {
        break;
      }
    }

    // 5. Add all newlyFilledTiles to filledTiles
    filledTiles.addAll(newlyFilledTiles);

    // 6. Update prevFilledDistance
    prevFilledDistance = distance;

    // 7. Update prevFilledTiles
    prevFilledTiles = newlyFilledTiles.size();

  private boolean isValidConnection(Cell neighborCell, int direction) {

      Pipe pipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
      if (pipe == null) {
        return false;
      }
      // Check if the pipe has an opening in the opposite direction

   *              - If nextCoord is within playable bounds [1..rows-2] x [1..cols-2]:

  public void fillTiles(final int distance)
  {
    // 1. If sourceCell is null or not filled, return.
    if (sourceCell == null || !sourceCell.isFilled()) {
      return;
    }

    // 2. Determine the new layer to fill.
    int prevDist = prevFilledDistance == null ? 0 : prevFilledDistance;
    if (distance <= prevDist) {
      return;
    }
    int stepsToAdd = distance - prevDist;

    // 3. Initialize BFS
    List<Coordinate> currentFrontier = new ArrayList<>(filledTiles);
    List<Coordinate> nextFrontier = new ArrayList<>();
    List<Coordinate> newlyFilledTiles = new ArrayList<>();

    // 4. Repeat 'stepsToAdd' times
    for (int step = 0; step < stepsToAdd; step++) {
      List<Coordinate> tempFrontier = new ArrayList<>();
      
      for (Coordinate coord : currentFrontier) {
        Cell cell = this.cell[coord.getRow()][coord.getCol()];
        
        // Determine connections
        List<Integer> connections = new ArrayList<>();
        if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
          Pipe pipe = ((FillableCell) cell).getPipe();
          if (pipe != null) {
            connections.addAll(pipe.getDirections()); // Assuming getDirections() or getConnections()
          }
        } else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
          // Termination cells might have a direction
          connections.add(((TerminationCell) cell).getDirection()); 
        }

        for (int d : connections) {
          Coordinate offset = Pa19Helper.getOffset(d);
          Coordinate nextCoord = coord.add(offset);

          // Check bounds
          if (nextCoord.isValid(getRows(), getCols())) { // Assuming isValid checks [1, rows-2] etc.
            // If not, manual check:
            if (nextCoord.getRow() >= 1 && nextCoord.getRow() < getRows() - 1 &&
                nextCoord.getCol() >= 1 && nextCoord.getCol() < getCols() - 1) {
              
              Cell neighborCell = this.cell[nextCoord.getRow()][nextCoord.getCol()];

              // Check if already filled
              if (!isFilled(nextCoord)) {
                
                // Check connection validity
                if (isValidConnection(neighborCell, d)) {
                  nextFrontier.add(nextCoord);
                  newlyFilledTiles.add(nextCoord);
                  
                  // Mark as filled
                  if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                     Pipe neighborPipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
                     if (neighborPipe != null) {
                       neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
                     }
                  } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                     ((TerminationCell) neighborCell).setFilled(true);
                  }
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
      
      currentFrontier = nextFrontier;
      nextFrontier = new ArrayList<>(); // Reset nextFrontier for next step
      
      if (currentFrontier.isEmpty()) {
        break;
      }
    }

    // 5. Add all newlyFilledTiles to filledTiles
    filledTiles.addAll(newlyFilledTiles);

    // 6. Update prevFilledDistance
    prevFilledDistance = distance;

    // 7. Update prevFilledTiles
    prevFilledTiles = newlyFilledTiles.size();
  }

  /**
   * Helper method to check if a neighbor cell is valid for connection in direction d
   * @LLM */
  private boolean isValidConnection(Cell neighborCell, int direction) {
    if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
      Pipe pipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
      if (pipe == null) {
        return false;
      }
      // Check if the pipe has an opening in the opposite direction
      int oppositeDirection = Pa19Helper.getOppositeDirection(direction);
      return pipe.getDirections().contains(oppositeDirection);
    } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
      // TerminationCell connects if its direction matches the incoming direction
      // Or if it's a sink/source that accepts water
      int neighborDir = ((TerminationCell) neighborCell).getDirection();
      return neighborDir == Pa19Helper.getOppositeDirection(direction);
    }
    return false;
  }

        if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
          Pipe pipe = ((FillableCell) cell).getPipe();
          if (pipe != null) {
            connections.addAll(pipe.getDirections()); // Assuming getDirections() or getConnections()
          }
        } else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
          // Termination cells might have a direction
          connections.add(((TerminationCell) cell).getDirection()); 
        }

        for (int d : connections) {
          Coordinate offset = Pa19Helper.getOffset(d);
          Coordinate nextCoord = coord.add(offset);

          // Check bounds
          if (nextCoord.isValid(getRows(), getCols())) { // Assuming isValid checks [1, rows-2] etc.
            // If not, manual check:
            if (nextCoord.getRow() >= 1 && nextCoord.getRow() < getRows() - 1 &&
                nextCoord.getCol() >= 1 && nextCoord.getCol() < getCols() - 1) {
              
              Cell neighborCell = this.cell[nextCoord.getRow()][nextCoord.getCol()];

              // Check if already filled
              if (!isFilled(nextCoord)) {
                
                // Check connection validity
                if (isValidConnection(neighborCell, d)) {
                  nextFrontier.add(nextCoord);
                  newlyFilledTiles.add(nextCoord);
                  
                  // Mark as filled
                  if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
                     Pipe neighborPipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
                     if (neighborPipe != null) {
                       neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
                     }
                  } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                     ((TerminationCell) neighborCell).setFilled(true);
                  }
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
      
      currentFrontier = nextFrontier;
      nextFrontier = new ArrayList<>(); // Reset nextFrontier for next step
      
      if (currentFrontier.isEmpty()) {
        break;
      }
    }

    // 5. Add all newlyFilledTiles to filledTiles
    filledTiles.addAll(newlyFilledTiles);

    // 6. Update prevFilledDistance
    prevFilledDistance = distance;

    // 7. Update prevFilledTiles
    prevFilledTiles = newlyFilledTiles.size();
  }

  /**
   * Helper method to check if a neighbor cell is valid for connection in direction d
   * @LLM */
  private boolean isValidConnection(Cell neighborCell, int direction) {
    if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell) {
      Pipe pipe = ((FillableCell) neighborCell).getPipe();
      if (pipe == null) {
        return false;
      }
      // Check if the pipe has an opening in the opposite direction
      int oppositeDirection = Pa19Helper.getOppositeDirection(direction);
      return pipe.getDirections().contains(oppositeDirection);
    } else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
      // TerminationCell connects if its direction matches the incoming direction
      // Or if it's a sink/source that accepts water
      int neighborDir = ((TerminationCell) neighborCell).getDirection();
      return neighborDir == Pa19Helper.getOppositeDirection(direction);
    }
    return false;
  }

            // If not, manual check:
